rows.name: spoken-why-warps-frozen-5
rows.question: Why
rows.answer: Because threads in a CUDA warp share instruction issue, they work most efficiently when following the same path. If they diverge, the GPU executes the different paths with nonparticipating threads inactive, reducing useful parallel work. Consecutive memory accesses can also be combined into fewer memory transactions, improving throughput.

rows.question: Y
rows.answer: Interpreting “Y” as “why”: a circular array gives the capacity-17 FIFO constant-time push and pop without shifting elements or allocating memory. Tracking the number of stored items distinguishes empty from full, allowing all 17 slots to be used and rejecting overflow. Wrapping the read and write indices modulo 17 preserves FIFO order as slots are reused.
